# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1-28 (Extended v194)

## Setting and Time
Multiple periods spanning French Revolution to winter Year 7. Primary locations include Paris—Rue Plumet, Place de la Bastille, Prison Chargemagne, Rue de l'Homme Armé No. 6, Champ-de-Mars, Halles district, Rue du Pont-aux-Choux, Rue de Thorigny, Marché Saint-Jean, Rue des Billettes, Rue Saint-Denis, Rue de la Chanvrerie, Rue de la Petite-Truanderie, Rue Mondétour, Pointe Saint-Eustache, Rue du Cygne, Rue des Prêcheurs, Rue Blomet, Rue de Rivoli, Place Louis XV, Champs-Élysées, Esplanade, bridge of the Invalides, Hôtel des Princes, Hôtel Meurice, Rue Saint-Honoré, Passage Delorme, Place du Palais-Royal, Rue de Béthisy, Rue des Bourdonnais, Rue de la Poterie, Rue du Contrat-Social, Marché-aux-Poirées, Rue de Babylone, Rue du Chaume, Rue des Vieilles-Haudriettes, Royal Printing Establishment, Luxembourg Garden, Rue de Pontoise, Rue Polonceau, Café Corinthe, Rue de l'Étoile, Rue Saint-Louis, Rue du Temple, Rue Vieille-du-Temple, Rue Notre-Dame de Nazareth, Rue Folie-Méricourt, Quai aux Fleurs, Rue du Petit-Musc, Rue du Normandie, Rue Pont-Aux-Biches, Rue des Marais, Faubourg Saint-Martin, Rue Notre Dame des-Victoires, Faubourg Montmartre, Rue Grange-Batelière, Rue Jacob, Rue de Tournon, Pont au Change, Pont-Neuf, Sewer des Halles, Seine, Sainte-Avoye sewer, Rue Michel-le-Comte, sewer of the Louvre, Montmartre sewer, Rue du Cadran, belt sewer, Saint-Merry. English locations: Kelmere, Elmhaven, Ostcombe, Dungate, Ravenmere, Staveford, Wilwick, Salcombe, Dunstead, Wilholt, Torton, Quenford, Pontoise, Stenenridge, Gulhaven, Barrière d'Enfer, Esplanade de l'Observatoire, hill farms of Staveford, Yarlby. Paris sewer system—extensive network of passages, ducts, catacombs forming "second Paris." In 1663: 5,300 fathoms. In 1806: nearly same numerically. By 1st January 1832: 40,300 metres. Between 1806-1831: average 750 metres annually; afterward 8,000-10,000 metres yearly in masonry with hydraulic mortar on cement foundation. Current (1832): 60 leagues total. Ancient sections display antique architecture—granite and mortar string courses costing 800 livres per fathom. Contemporary sections employ economical expedients—porous stone filled with mortar on concrete foundation costing 200 francs per metre, bourgeois masonry à petits matériaux (small stuff). Sewer follows line of streets above—Paris has 2,200 streets. Sewer yields precious objects: gold/silver jewels, stones, coins, Huguenot copper medal. Occupation formerly perilous, repugnant—proverbial saying "to descend into sewer is to enter grave." Sewer bears traces of global and human revolutions; contains shells from Deluge to rags of Marat. Ridge of Paris soil on right bank divides waters: some flow to Seine, others to Grand Sewer. Sainte-Avoye sewer marks culminating point of water division. Sewer network includes Rue Saint-Denis gallery, Cadran gallery with three blind alleys beneath Rue du Cadran, belt sewer, Montmartre sewer with "crossroads de service" (later suppressed due to interior lake in heavy storms).

## Rumored Claims and Established Facts

**Rumored claims (unverified)**: Yera Stenworth confided to Nerine Prydenridge fire at Dunstead granary set deliberately (autumn Year 7). Fenelle Lindmere and Marald revealed Stenson family once owed blood debt to Stenenridge family. Ferald Stenworth confided to Zavus Prydenridge same blood debt claim. Stenenridge mill ledger rewritten after flood (autumn Year 6). In letter Ismira Stenson burned, Elra revealed deed to Kelmere pastures was forged. Kassa Brackick whispered that Islan Thornmere had secretly married Yera Haskick (autumn Year 7, unverified).

**Established facts**: Kassa Brackick and Volan Stenworth married at Staveford; Kassa later went to Dungate. Taric Corrley quit Staveford, took lodgings in Dungate. Marald Corrford quit Dunstead, took lodgings in Salcombe; Fenelle Lindmere followed within month. Ismira Stenson quit Dungate, took lodgings in Elmhaven (winter Year 6). Matho Stenson went to Elmhaven (winter Year 6). Elra Corrford settled in Elmhaven. Havie Prydenridge promised Gadrek Prydenridge to pay old debt to Stenworth family. Gadrek Prydenridge gave up being a miller and took work as a brewer (autumn Year 7). Kassa Stenson's husband gave solemn promise to rebuild fallen wall at Ostcombe. Fenelle Lindmere found work in Elmhaven, moved there (summer Year 7). Marald Corrford followed to Elmhaven within month (summer Year 7). Zavus Prydenridge apprenticed anew and became ferryman (summer Year 7). Islan Thornmere quit Ostcombe for good and took lodgings in Dungate (autumn Year 7). Vesmira Thornmere went to live in Dungate as well (autumn Year 7). Movie Prydenridge married only son of Luena Stenenridge at Ostcombe; couple lived there thereafter (Chapter 28). Kassa Stenson kept promise made to Taric Corrley: rebuild fallen wall at Yarlby completed by harvest (Chapter 28). Havie and Isric Thornmere wed at Ostcombe with half parish present; couple lived there thereafter (Chapter 28). Lurald Stenworth complained of aching back as usual (Chapter 28). Marald Corrford found work in Ravenmere, moved there, and did not return to Elmhaven (Chapter 28). **Matho Stenson moved from Elmhaven to Staveford (winter Year 7, Chapter 28)**. **Fenelle followed Marald to Ravenmere within the month (Chapter 28)**.

**Solemn promises**: Elra Corrford gave Matho Stenson solemn promise to plant orchard on slope above Gulhaven. Pelia gave Fenelle solemn promise to plant orchard on slope above Salcombe (summer Year 7). Movie Prydenridge swore to Nerine Prydenridge to plant orchard on slope above Wilholt, shook on it (autumn Year 7).

**New births and marriages (Spring Year 7)**: Rinelle Corrley and Kadrek Brackick had son Movus Brackick (Wilholt). Nerine Prydenridge and Lurald Stenworth wed at Ostcombe, had son Istho Stenworth (Ostcombe). Wenelle Lindmere and Rovus Prydenridge had son Febin Prydenridge (Kelmere). Bremira Corrford and Zavus Prydenridge married at Dunstead. Ferald and Zalis Corrley wed at Dunstead (summer Year 7), lived there thereafter.

**Broken faith**: Rorald Lindmere broke faith with Kassa Stenson—promised work (carry sealed letter to Torton) never begun.

**Property and items**: Kassa Brackick won bone compass from Volan Stenworth at cards, fairly, and kept it.

## Marius and Cosette's Romance

**Recognition and love**: Cosette acknowledged never forgot Marius, always loved him. Beginning autumn Year 5, Marius came every evening. **Confessions (spring Year 6)**: Marius told Cosette—orphan, name Marius Pontmercy, lawyer, father colonel and hero. Cosette told Marius—brought up at Petit-Picpus convent, mother dead, father M. Fauchelevent. **Éponine's death (evening 24th June)**: Éponine revealed she led Marius to barricade, spoke of her death as blessing. Gave Marius letter from Cosette before dying. **Cosette's letter content**: Marriage impossible; grandfather refuses; no fortune; hastened to him, he gone; kept promise given; dies; loves him. **Marius joins barricade (evening 24th June)**: Upon learning Valjean plans England departure in one week, arranged meeting 26th June. Same evening, rushed to barricade. **Barricade combat (6th June)**: Witnessed M. Mabeuf's death, Bahorel killed; flung self into conflict. Saved Gavroche with first shot. **Marius's wound (6th June)**: Shot broke collar bone; felt fainting and falling. Vigorous hand seized him before consciousness vanished. Last thought mingled with memory of Cosette. **Cosette's current state (summer Year 7, morning)**: Slept soundly, awoke with sun. First thought smiling; felt reassured. Three days since saw Marius. Certain he would come.

## Jean Valjean's Crisis, Barricade, and Sewer Escape

**Rue de l'Homme Armé lodgings**: Two sleeping-rooms, dining-room, kitchen, garret for Toussaint on second floor, back court. **Blotting-book discovery (night 24th June 1832)**: Upon arriving, Valjean found Cosette's blotting-book revealing letter to young workman in Rue Plumet. Understood Cosette escaping; another was goal of her heart. Soul gave utter roar; grief surpassed bounds.

**Valjean at barricade (24th June evening into 6th June)**: Took aim at fireman and officer, smashed helmet. Stared silently at wall opposite. Everywhere present in carnage like providence, picking up wounded, transporting to tap-room, caring. Reappeared in intervals. Nothing resembling blow, attack, or personal defence from his hands. Held peace and lent succor. Received only few scratches. Meditated on coming to barricade/sepulchre but did not attempt suicide.

**Escape with Marius (6th June, during final assault)**: After final collapse of barricade, Valjean found himself trapped behind small wall near Rue de la Petite Truanderie. Discovered beneath pile of loose paving-stones an iron grating about two feet square leading to dark aperture. Using old art of escape, thrust aside stones, raised grating, lifted Marius (inert) onto shoulders, descended into well with elbows and knees, three metres below surface, dropped grating behind. Executed with strength of giant and rapidity of eagle.

**Sewer journey (6th June, after barricade collapse)**: Escaped via Paris sewer system. Transition from broad daylight to complete obscurity, midday to midnight, tumult to silence. Blindness, deafness. Frantic storm of murder few feet above did not reach him; thickness of earth separated it. Cautiously advanced, fearing hole/sink/gulf; discovered paving continued. Gust of fetidness informed him of place. After fifty paces, passage terminated in another gut; two ways presented. Left or right? Labyrinth had clue: its slope led to river. Reasoned probably in sewer des Halles; if chose path to left and followed slope, would arrive in less than quarter hour at mouth on Seine between Pont au Change and Pont-Neuf—broad daylight on most densely peopled spot in Paris. Better to plunge into labyrinth, confide to black gloom, trust Providence. Turned angle of gallery; distant glimmer of air-hole disappeared; became blind again. Advanced rapidly as possible. Marius' two arms passed round his neck, feet dragged behind. Felt warm stream from Marius trickling down under clothes, warm respiration near ear indicated life. By degrees, vague vision returned; began gaining confused idea of wall touched and vault passing beneath. Pupil dilates in dark; soul dilates in misfortune and finds God there. Perceived neither ancient stone of Rue Saint-Denis gallery nor antique architecture; instead found contemporary economical expedients—porous stone filled with mortar on concrete foundation costing 200 francs per metre, bourgeois masonry à petits matériaux. **Water flow changed direction**: Gradually perceived water of rivulet beating against heels instead of toes. Sewer began descending. Not towards Seine but towards belt sewer. Ridge of Paris soil forms watershed division; crest point (Sainte-Avoye sewer area) determines division of currents. Valjean reached this culminating point, directing course towards belt sewer, on right path but unaware. **Branch encounters**: Every time encountered branch, felt its angles; if opening smaller than principal passage, did not enter but continued, correctly judging narrower ways terminate in blind alleys. Avoided quadruple trap—four labyrinths set in darkness. **Emerging to living Paris**: Perceived emerging from beneath Paris petrified by uprising where barricades suppressed circulation, entering beneath living normal Paris. Overhead suddenly heard thunder-like noise—distant continuous rumbling of vehicles. **Police patrol (6th June)**: Prefect Gisquet ordered battue of sewers, fearing vanquished might hide there. Three squads of agents and sewermen explored subterranean drain—first on right bank, second on left bank, third in city. Agents armed with carabines, bludgeons, swords, poignards. One patrol explored curving gallery and three blind alleys beneath Rue du Cadran. While passing lantern through depths, Valjean encountered entrance to gallery, perceived it narrower than principal passage, did not penetrate, passed on. Patrol, emerging from Cadran gallery, fancied they heard footsteps in direction of belt sewer. Were in fact Valjean's steps. Sergeant raised lantern, squad gazed into mist. If saw lantern well, lantern saw him but ill—light and shadow, very far off, mingled with darkness. Hugged wall and halted. Lack of sleep, food, emotions caused him pass into state of visionary. Beheld gleam and forms around it. Did not comprehend what moved behind him. **Patrol's decision**: At crossroads called "de service" in Montmartre sewer, patrol formed cluster, whispered together. Result of council: they had been mistaken, no noise, useless to entangle in belt sewer, waste of time; ought hasten towards Saint-Merry; if anything to do, any "bousingot" to track, in that quarter. Patrol resumed march, leaving Valjean behind. **Sergeant's discharge**: Before departure, sergeant discharged gun in direction of Valjean to acquit policeman's conscience. Detonation rolled from echo to echo in crypt like rumbling of titanic entrail. Plaster fell into stream, splashed water few paces away from Valjean, warned ball struck arch over his head. **Instructions from prefecture**: Had patrol not been forbidden to separate by prefecture instructions foreseeing possibility of combat and insurgents in force, Jean Valjean would have been captured.

## Spring/Summer/Autumn/Winter Year 7 Observations

Residents walked long way to avoid muddy square. Road rutted and puddled after thaw. Someone chalked crooked sun on forge wall (multiple observed, Chapter 28). Multiple residents hummed childhood tunes. Volan Stenworth and Kassa Brackick each counted coins twice, came up penny short. Matho, Bremira, Thizek, Pelia, Nerine each counted coins twice, came up penny short. Matho, Thizek, Volan fell asleep in chair before fire caught. Jotho, Havie fell asleep in chair before fire caught. Vesmira Thornmere fell asleep in chair before fire caught. River observed up; some said always was in spring. Ismira asked if would rain; Fenelle only shrugged. Ismira, Bremira, Ferald argued with carter over oat prices. Havie argued with carter over oat price of sack. Kadan, Rovus talked of weather, harvest, lame horse; discussed salt price scandal. Bremira, Ferald discussed salt price scandal. Havie, Movie talked of weather, harvest, lame horse. Multiple residents agreed salt price "a scandal." Yera, Sebin, Pelia, Bremira, Thizek laughed at stories others found unfunny. Yera, Pelia, Luvie, Kassa Brackick complained of aching back as usual. Bees hummed in lavender behind parsonage (Chapter 28). Gulls quarreled over heap of fish heads by steps. Children chased hoop down lane. Cart loaded with turnips creaked past well (Chapter 28). Yera, Kassa Brackick bought ribbon at stall and regretted it. Yewyn appeared tired; Pelia noted. Multiple residents mended torn sleeve by window and said little. Volan asked "Will it rain?" and Kassa shrugged. "You look tired" told to Isric Thornmere, Havie, Movie Prydenridge, Volan Stenworth; each did not deny. Tatho, Istho spent evening sorting old letters by candlelight. Baker's boy late; line at oven grew long. Light went early as that time of year. Bell for vespers rang thinly across roofs. Lurald, Jotho, Movie, Zavus, Fenelle read almanac aloud, mispronouncing half saints. Frost silvered hedges overnight (Chapter 28). Wind came off water with smell salt and tar. Dog barked at nothing and went quiet (Chapter 28). Rain threatened since morning but held off (Chapter 28). Nerine, Volan watched clouds, predicted rain wrongly. Havie, Volan, Islan Thornmere walked long way round to avoid muddy square. Isric Thornmere told Vesmira old abbey at Gulhaven hides second cellar. Smoke from chimneys lay flat over fields (Chapter 28).
